**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in POMT2 —DISRUPTS→ POMT2 (HGNC:9002); Pathogenic variant in POMGNT1 —DISRUPTS→ POMGNT1 (HGNC:9001); POMT2 (HGNC:9002) —BINDS→ Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0006479); POMGNT1 (HGNC:9001) —BINDS→ Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0006479); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0006479) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy with lens and retinal abnormalities (HP:0030763); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0006479) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000547). Loss-of-function variants in POMT2 cause Walker-Warburg syndrome, while loss-of-function variants in POMGNT1 cause retinitis pigmentosa 76. Both POMT2 and POMGNT1 are key enzymes in the protein O-mannosylation pathway. Disruption of this pathway by mutations in either gene leads to a spectrum of phenotypes, including congenital muscular dystrophy with lens and retinal abnormalities (for POMT2 mutations) and retinitis pigmentosa (for POMGNT1 mutations), reflecting the critical role of O-mannosylation in both muscle and retinal development and function.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in POMT2 are found to be common (e.g., >1% allele frequency in gnomAD) in individuals diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa 76 without other features of Walker-Warburg syndrome, or vice versa, it would suggest that the causal link is weaker or that other genetic factors play a more significant role in differentiating these specific disease presentations. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in POMT2 or POMGNT1 with allele frequency > 0.01)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of defective protein O-mannosylation in both Walker-Warburg syndrome and retinitis pigmentosa 76 opens avenues for therapeutic strategies. Targeting the O-mannosylation pathway or downstream consequences could potentially benefit patients with either condition, particularly in addressing the retinal phenotypes. Identifying patients with RP76 who might also have undiagnosed subclinical muscular or neurological issues related to POMT2 could lead to earlier diagnosis and management of a broader spectrum of O-mannosylation disorders.
